Subject: Renewal: need commit uplift + fallback for Q3 spike

Priyom / Karthik,

Hope you’re both well. We’re looking at a significant seasonal lift in Q3 driven by a new marketing funnel — our internal forecast shows a 3x increase in token consumption versus current monthly average.

We’re approaching our renewal and want to avoid production slowdowns. High-level ask:
- Move our hosted API monthly commit from 1.2B tokens to 3.5B (monthly) for the 12-month renewal term.
- A two-month soft oversubscribe buffer for unpredictable spikes (we’ll pay overage, but need a smoother throttling/fallback path).
- Confirmation of per-route rate limits and recommended guardrails for bursty traffic.

Attached is our recent usage export (current-usage.csv) to help. Can you share a pricing sketch + any operational caveats (latency SLO impact, rate limit gating behavior) so we can present to finance and infra?

Also please cc your procurement/legal contact for contract timing.

Thanks,
Daniel

EdgeCart

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal: need commit uplift + fallback for Q3 spike

Thanks for the context, Daniel — this is exactly the kind of renewal we design for. Quick response with a proposed path and the practical trade-offs.

Summary proposal (fast-read):
- Commit move: 1.2B --> 3.5B monthly for a 12-month renewal term.
- Pricing: discounted blended rate for the committed tokens + standard overage at published rate; sample pricing breakdown attached (proposal-tierstep.pdf).
- Soft oversubscribe buffer: we can enable a 60-day oversubscribe window where we will NOT automatic-throttle to hard cutoffs; instead requests above commit are met with a graduated soft-throttle and overflow routing to compatible model variants where appropriate. This preserves availability while we reconcile billing.
- Rate limits & per-route guidance: recommend per-route qps caps and adaptive client-side retry policy (we’ll include recommended settings in the SLO appendix).

Operational notes / caveats:
- Latency: during sustained bursts where autoscaling is triggered, p50 remains unchanged; p95 may increase by ~10-25ms depending on model choice. We’ll monitor and can enable preforked instances for critical routes if you want stricter p95 bounds.
- Billing/proration: we’ll prorate the commit for the first partial month; overages during the 60-day buffer will be billed monthly (no immediate enforcement).
- SLA exception: we can add a temporary burst SLA for the first 90 days of the term to smooth your rollout, subject to an agreed uplift fee.

Next steps (recommended):
1) Confirm acceptance of target commit (3.5B) and 12-month term.
2) I’ll route a formal amendment and price summary to your procurement contact and include a proposed DocuSign link.
3) Schedule a 30-min rollout call with infra (Karthik) + our SRE to walk through guardrails and routing.

I attached a short proposal PDF with numbers and an appendix with recommended per-route caps. If that looks good I’ll pull legal in and prepare the amendment (we can mock a DocuSign today).

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal: need commit uplift + fallback for Q3 spike

Looping in operational constraints — quick bullets: 
- Soft oversubscribe behavior: we implement graduated throttles based on rolling 1m/5m token ingress. For EdgeCart's expected 3x bump, recommend per-route qps caps: default 600 rps per route, burst 1,200 rps for 60s.
- Fallback routing: define a small percentage (5-10%) of traffic eligible for model-variant fallback (cheaper, quantized) when commit thresholds are crossed. That protects latency-sensitive routes.
- Caching: enable prefix KV caching for idempotent completions (we can reduce token burn by ~8-12% in practice).
- Instrumentation: require a short rollout snippet to tag high-priority routes so we can prioritize prewarmed capacity.

If EdgeCart agrees we’ll add the rate caps to the amendment and produce a short ops-runbook for your SREs.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infra Ops, Redwood Inference
